column1: # note: Liftoff v1.6.3 (conda env liftoff; its minimap2 2.24), self-lift of each genome's RefSeq gene + pseudogene records: -copies -sc 0.95 -a 0.5 -s 0.5 -overlap 0.1 -p 4 -f pseudogene; default -mm2_options (-a --end-bonus 5 --eqx -N 50 -p 0.5)
# note: run as one Liftoff call per contig's records (blocks of <= 2500 records) against the WHOLE genome; cross-call overlaps resolved by Liftoff's own rule (prereg §1 M1-M3)

# note: V-L1 (mini-genome chr20-22, one Liftoff run vs per-contig calls and vs blocks of records; prereg amendment 3): B_contigs: 3740 of 3750 annotated placements identical, 439 of 448 extra copies identical (Jaccard 0.9799) -> FAIL: reported as an approximation of one run; C_blocks: 3730 of 3750 annotated placements identical, 438 of 449 extra copies identical (Jaccard 0.9755) -> FAIL: reported as an approximation of one run
# note: matching (prereg §3): cov(G|R) = |exons(G) ∩ exons(R)| / |exons(G)| >= 0.5, same contig, strand ignored; in one genome Liftoff's sequence_ID of a coordinate match equals its coverage

# note: reference loci: Liftoff in_place / moved / extra_copy with exon union >= 200 bp and >= 2 reads of the sample whose primary alignment (-F 2308) has an aligned block on the exon union (the rule of Fig. 6d); sens_* = k of n covered >= 50% by one Rustle locus

# note: denovo = gene_id groups of the sample's genome-wide assembly (run cache stage assemble; exon union of every transcript); families = the DEFAULT de novo families' copy table (run cache stage families, <id>.fam.copies.tsv: one copy per member locus of a family, its representative's exons; prereg amendment 5); catalog = the LEGACY copy catalog (stage catalog, its exons column; secondary, no claim, not drawn)

# note: located = Rustle loci covered >= 50% by one placed Liftoff locus (the rest lie outside every Liftoff locus: not an error); pair_cofamily = claim F1 (families; the catalog rows are the legacy comparison)
# note: scope minus_dev: without the development contigs (human chr16; gorilla chr20 = NC_073244.2); chimpanzee and orangutan have none
# note: 95% intervals: 2,000 bootstrap resamples of source records (random seed 20260925)
